items.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: My band in Richmond, we became a really popular back-up band for black artists... James Brown had his big 18 piece band... I get chills just thinking about that, when I first saw that 18 piece

ctx.x: That’s good info. Well I’ve got to get in a thing about — I know you’re passionate about black music and how it affected bringing the races together.

I taught a course at Vanderbilt for eight years, it’s called Rhythm & Blues Tore Down the Walls of Segregation. I’m teaching it now at Virginia/Wesleyan in Virginia Beach where © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-

I live now. I taught it at Vanderbilt for eight years. But yeah, very passionate about that. Because I lived through it in the 60s. My band in Richmond, we became a really popular back-up band for black artists. Back then there were very few artists that carried bands. James Brown had his big 18 piece band and they were like a machine. I get chills just thinking about that, when I first saw that 18 piece, that curtain open up and those guys are in tuxedos.
